_comment: Theory cards for the chord library, keyed by chord quality id.

maj7.title: Major seventh
maj7.sound: Warm, settled, luminous. The sound of arriving home.
maj7.function: Tonic (I) and subdominant (IV) chords in major keys, and the bVI/bIII chords borrowed into minor keys. Interchangeable with 6 and 6/9 on tonics.
maj7.listen: Fly Me to the Moon (Cmaj7, Fmaj7), Autumn Leaves (Bbmaj7, Ebmaj7)

6.title: Major sixth
6.sound: Older, sweeter, more swing-era than maj7. No leading-tone rub between 7 and root.
6.function: Tonic chords, especially when the melody sits on the root. Swing-era charts write I6 where later charts write Imaj7.
6.listen: All of Me (C6), Take the A Train (C6)

69.title: Six-nine
69.sound: Open, glassy, unresolved-but-at-rest. The classic final chord of a jazz tune.
69.function: Tonic. A 6/9 voicing avoids both the major 7th and the 5th, which is why it sounds so spacious.
69.listen: Ending chords everywhere, especially Wes Montgomery.

maj9.title: Major ninth
maj9.sound: Maj7 with a softer, more modern top.
maj9.function: Any place a maj7 works. Use when the melody note is the 9th.

maj7#11.title: Major seventh sharp eleven
maj7#11.sound: Lydian brightness: floating, slightly tense, dreamy.
maj7#11.function: IV chords in major keys (the #11 is diatonic there) and bII or bVI chords used as colour.
maj7#11.listen: Take the A Train bar 3 (the D7#11 is the dominant cousin).

m.title: Minor triad
m.function: Rare on jazz charts by itself; usually read as m7 or m6 depending on context.
m.listen: Pop and folk more than jazz.

m6.title: Minor sixth
m6.sound: Dark but stable: the minor tonic that does not want to move on.
m6.function: Tonic minor (i6). Also the top four notes of a 9 chord a fourth away, which is why it appears as a substitute for dominants (Fm6 = Bb9 without the root).

m69.title: Minor six-nine
m69.sound: m6 with a brighter top: the gypsy-jazz and Wes minor tonic.

m7.title: Minor seventh
m7.sound: Soft, flowing, wants to move (usually down a fifth).
m7.function: The ii chord of the ii–V–I. Also iii, vi, and tonic minor in modal tunes.
m7.listen: Autumn Leaves (Cm7 → F7), Blue Bossa (Cm7, Fm7)

m9.title: Minor ninth
m9.sound: m7 with more air on top.
m9.function: Any ii chord. The 9th is almost always available on a ii chord.
m9.listen: Comping over ii–V–Is in a modern style.

m11.title: Minor eleventh
m11.function: Modal minor tonics and ii chords when the melody is on the 11th.

mMaj7.title: Minor-major seventh
mMaj7.sound: Film-noir tension: minor with a leading tone inside it.
mMaj7.function: Tonic minor, especially descending lines i – i(maj7) – i7 – i6.
mMaj7.listen: Line clichés over minor tonics (My Funny Valentine is the classic).

m11b5.title: Half-diminished eleventh
m11b5.sound: Half-diminished with the 11th on top: less bleak, more modern.
m11b5.function: Any iiø7 chord; the 11th is the target key's tonic note.

7.title: Dominant seventh
7.sound: Unstable, driving. The tritone between 3 and b7 wants to resolve.
7.function: V of the key or of any other chord (secondary dominants). Also the tonic sound of the blues.
7.listen: F Blues (all of it), Autumn Leaves (F7, D7)

9.title: Dominant ninth
9.function: Any unaltered dominant, particularly in blues and swing.

13.title: Dominant thirteenth
13.function: V7 resolving to a major chord; the 13th is the target chord's 3rd.
13.listen: Fly Me to the Moon (G13 → Cmaj7)

7b9.title: Dominant flat nine
7b9.function: V7 resolving to a MINOR chord (V7b9 → i). The top four notes form a dim7 chord.

7#9.title: Dominant sharp nine
7#9.sound: Gritty, bluesy: the major and minor third at once.

7#5.title: Dominant sharp five
7#5.function: V7 resolving to major or minor; also the last chord of a bar before a ii chord.

7b5.title: Dominant flat five
7b5.sound: Ambiguous: it is its own tritone substitute.
7b5.function: V7 or its tritone sub; the same shape moved six frets gives the same notes.

7#11.title: Dominant sharp eleven
7#11.function: II7 chords (the D7 in Take the A Train), bVII7, and tritone substitutes.

7b13.title: Dominant flat thirteen
7b13.sound: Minor-key dominant colour with a sighing top note.
7b13.function: V7 in minor keys; b13 is the minor key's b6.

7alt.title: Altered dominant
7alt.sound: Maximum tension. Every extension is flattened or sharpened.
7alt.function: V7 resolving down a fifth, usually to a minor chord or for maximum drama into a major one.

7sus4.title: Dominant suspended fourth
7sus4.sound: Open, gospel, no third. Suspended but not tense.
7sus4.function: V7sus4 → V7 → I, or as a stand-alone modal chord.
7sus4.listen: Herbie Hancock's Maiden Voyage (sus chords all the way).

9sus4.title: Dominant ninth suspended
9sus4.sound: 7sus4 with a wider top; equals a m7 chord a fifth up over the root.
9sus4.listen: Modern comping over long dominant pedals.

sus4.title: Suspended fourth
sus4.function: Delays the third of a triad; resolves to major or minor.
sus4.listen: Pop more than jazz, but useful in intros.

m7b5.title: Half-diminished (minor seven flat five)
m7b5.sound: Sad, leaning, unresolved. Minor's darker cousin.
m7b5.function: The ii chord of a MINOR ii–V–i (iiø7 – V7b9 – i). Also viiø7 in major.
m7b5.listen: Autumn Leaves (Am7b5 → D7 → Gm), Fly Me to the Moon (Bm7b5 → E7 → Am7)

dim.title: Diminished triad
dim.function: Usually read as dim7 on jazz charts.

dim7.title: Diminished seventh
dim7.sound: Symmetrical, spooky, spinning. Every note can be the root.
dim7.function: Passing chord between diatonic chords (I – #Idim7 – ii), or a rootless 7b9 (Bdim7 = G7b9 without the G).
dim7.listen: F Blues bar 6 (Bdim7), All of Me turnaround (Ebdim7)
